content:
emily.sales: quick sync — Weaver Health POC: they ran our smokebench and reported intermittent tail latency and 5xxs when qps > 120. Sales asked for a short runbook + cost estimate and any security blockers. can we triage?

raj.seng: ok — thanks. can someone paste their exact workload shape? avg tokens / request, model, and if they do streaming? that changes batching behavior.

tom.weaver: hi team — thanks. typical traffic: 60% small prompts (~120 tokens), 30% medium (~600 tokens), 10% long (~2000 tokens). using chat completions w/ streaming off for now. goal is sustained 150 qps with occasional bursts to 250 for 2–3 minutes.

maya.ops: noted. security side: they asked about KMS for key material and SSO mapping for audit. also need clarifications on VPC/private deployment latency impact. i can draft answers but need POC model choices and expected token counts per second to size.

raj.seng: got it. initial hypothesis: tail latency and 5xxs at >120 qps likely due to batching threshold + queue depth hitting our per-GPU concurrency cap. propose a two-step POC: 1) controlled load sweep to reproduce, 2) repeat with prefix caching enabled and a slightly different batching window.

raj.seng: suggested runbook (short):
- phase A: baseline smoke (10m) — 50/100/150 qps steady, collect p50/p95/p99 + error rates
- phase B: burst test (3m bursts) — ramp 150 -> 250 over 30s, hold 3m, cool down 2m
- phase C: config test — enable prefix KV cache + reduce batching window to 15ms, repeat phase A/B
- metrics: tokens/s, GPU util, queue depth, serve latency (p50/p95/p99), 5xx traces

raj.seng: load generator snippet (k6-like) for ops: 
```
export default function () {
  http.post('https://redwood.example/v1/chat:generate', JSON.stringify({
    model: 'rwd-open-chat-3b',
    input: genPrompt(),
  }), { headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer $POC_KEY', 'Content-Type':'application/json' } })
}
```

emily.sales: pricing ask — they want a rough delta between hosted vs dedicated for sustained 150 qps. can we give quick ballpark (monthly) and whether burst to 250 needs dedicated reserve?

raj.seng: rough numbers: hosted at this sustained QPS for rwd-open-chat-3b -> estimate ~X tokens/s -> cost ~ $12k/mo (usage). Dedicated (reserved single pool for this tenant, 2x A100 equiv) -> ~$9k/mo reserved + infra ops add-on. bursts: if they need deterministic headroom, dedicated with burst buffer is better; otherwise hosted can handle bursts but with fallback to cheaper model variants occasionally. I'll follow up with more precise calc after we run a small benchmark.

maya.ops: security notes for answering questionnaire:
- KMS: we support customer KMS via our private deployment or Dedicated (bring-your-own-key supported). hosted supports envelope encryption and HSM integration for enterprise tiers.
- SSO: SAML/OIDC available; audit logs exportable to SIEM for Dedicated/Private.
- Data residency: we have region pinning and private control plane for Private customers.

tom.weaver: thanks — prefer hosted first then evaluate Dedicated if price/perf favors. also any prewarm or coldstart recommendations? cold starts show up in our runs at the start of bursts.

raj.seng: prewarm suggestions: use a small steady background traffic (5–10 qps) to keep KV caches warm. for streaming vs non-streaming: streaming reduces client-perceived tail but increases overall resource usage. also we should test path where model falls back to quantized variant; that can reduce tail but slightly change outputs.

infra-bot: deploy success: canary rwd-open-chat-3b@hash-0a1b2c rolled to staging in 3m 12s — perf telemetry enabled.

raj.seng: run coordination: who can own the baseline run tomorrow at 09:00 PT? i'll set up a dashboard with p50/p95/p99, queue depth, gpu util, and error traces.

emily.sales: i can coordinate with Weaver and confirm 09:00 PT. tom, i'll DM calendar invite and put expected traffic profile.

tom.weaver: confirmed — 09:00 PT works. we'll provide PII-free test prompts and example payloads.

maya.ops: i'll prefill the security appendix answers and attach KMS/OIDC docs. also will note Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for audit logs.

raj.seng: action items:
- raj.seng: prepare load scripts + dashboard (today EOD)
- maya.ops: draft security questionnaire answers + docs (tomorrow AM)
- emily.sales: lock calendar and send invites to tom + weaver stakeholders
- tom.weaver: provide sample prompts and token distribution file

emily.sales: thanks team — i'll include a quick ballpark pricing line in the invite so their procurement has something to chew on. :thumbsup:

tom.weaver: appreciated. looking forward to root-cause and numbers.

emily.sales: will update thread after first run with numbers and next steps.
